# Configuration and command-line reference

<!-- Generated by tool/generate_configuration_reference.dart. Do not edit by hand. -->

This reference is generated from Dart Terminal’s typed configuration schema. Option names, syntax, defaults, repeatability, and application policies must therefore match `--help`, `--show-config`, and the native Settings inspector.

## Process modes

- `--help` prints schema-generated usage without reading config.
- `--show-config` resolves configuration and prints the bounded `dart-terminal-effective-config` version 1 document without starting the terminal application.
- `--show-config` may be combined with `--config=PATH`, `--no-config`, and the schema options below. It cannot be combined with `--help` or integration-only runtime arguments.

## Files, syntax, and precedence

The default file is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dart-terminal/config`, or `~/Library/Application Support/Dart Terminal/config` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset. A missing default file is ignored. Use `--config=PATH` for an explicit file or `--no-config` to skip files.

Files are UTF-8 `name = value` assignments. Blank lines and comments are accepted; quote values containing spaces or `#`. `include` paths are resolved relative to the including file. Precedence is schema default, included files, including file, then command line.

Resolution is bounded to 32 files, include depth 8, 1048576 bytes per file, 16384 UTF-16 units per line, 4096 assignments, and 128 diagnostics.

## Diagnostics and migration

File diagnostics retain severity, stable code, path, line, column, and a repair hint when available. Error-bearing startup snapshots recover to the last valid value or schema default. Error-bearing reload candidates are rejected atomically; warning-only candidates are accepted.

A syntactically valid file value that is unavailable to the current application also reports `CFG_UNAVAILABLE_VALUE` and uses that option’s schema default for startup. For example, an unavailable `font-family` starts with `system`. The original file text remains available in Settings for correction. Explicit command-line values are not silently changed.

The compatibility spelling `theme = default` resolves to `system` but emits `CFG_DEPRECATED_VALUE`; replace it with `theme = system`. Canonical effective output always reports `system`.

## Keybindings and actions

The repeatable `keybind` option uses `chord=target`. Physical key names, modifier ordering, pane/application action IDs, standard bindings, and reserved native shortcuts are generated separately in [Keybindings and actions](keybindings-and-actions.md).
